claims.claim_ar: يجوز أن تكون جملة «مَنْ يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ...» مبتدأً وخبرًا
claims.claim_en: It is permissible to analyze the clause 'man yashri nafsahu...' as a mubtada' (subject) and khabar (predicate).
claims.needs_review_reason: The source example discusses «مِنْهُمْ مَنْ ...»; applying the same acceptability to «مِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ ...» is a generalization that should be checked against the specific context of this āyah.

claims.source_quote_ar: يَجُوزُ أَنْ يكون مِنْهُم رَافعا لمن

claims.claim_ar: يجوز أن تؤخذ الجملة «مَنْ يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ...» نعتًا (صيغة وصفية للجملة التي قبلها في السياق المشابه)
claims.claim_en: The clause can be taken as a na't (adjectival/descriptive clause) modifying the preceding noun (in the cited discussion it modifies 'rasulīn').
claims.needs_review_reason: Source explicitly says the clause is a na't for 'rusul' in its example; applying 'na't' reading to the present verse (where the preceding noun is 'al-nās') is a contextual generalization that needs verification.

claims.claim_ar: يجوز أن تكون الجملة «مَنْ يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ...» مستأنفة (مستقلة مُستأنفًا عنها السياق السابق)
claims.claim_en: It is permissible to analyze the clause 'man yashri nafsahu...' as an independent resumed clause (musta'naf).
claims.needs_review_reason: The source treats this option in the context of a different example; confirm that treating the clause as musta'naf suits the syntactic relationship in this particular āyah.
